1.title: The Remaining Five of the Granite Family
1.items.0.label: Brand (Turckheim, 57.95 ha)
1.items.0.desc: Legend calls it the "place where the sun fought the dragon", famous since the Middle Ages. Sandy soils weathered from Turckheim two-mica granite. Riesling, Pinot Gris and Gewurztraminer are all excellent, with delicate, refined wines and imperial, elegant balance.
1.items.1.label: Frankstein (Dambach-la-Ville, 56.20 ha)
1.items.1.desc: Weathered two-mica granite sand, facing east and southeast, with very early sun. Widely renowned in the Middle Ages: both the Unterlinden convent in Colmar and Strasbourg cathedral once owned vineyards here (1320). Suited to Riesling and Gewurztraminer, showing best after several years in bottle.
1.items.2.label: Winzenberg (Blienschwiller, 19.20 ha)
1.items.2.desc: Two-mica granite on a steep south-southeast slope with very long sunshine hours. Riesling, Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris all suit it, with delicate, elegant floral wines and excellent ageing potential.
1.items.3.label: Praelatenberg (Kintzheim, 18.70 ha)
1.items.3.desc: Overlooked by Haut-Kœnigsbourg castle. Metamorphic gneiss base with heavy siliceous soil full of iron-rich gravel, well-drained and quick to warm. Documented as early as 823. Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Muscat and Pinot Gris are all fine, showing delicacy and elegance with age.
1.items.4.label: Gloeckelberg (Rodern & Saint-Hippolyte, 23.40 ha)
1.items.4.desc: Granite bedrock with acidic, sandy brown soils, locally more clayey through contact with Carboniferous schist / sandstone. Mainly Pinot Gris and Gewurztraminer, owned by monasteries since the Middle Ages, with delicate, light, elegant wines and lasting aromas.
2.question: What is the legendary origin of the site name Brand (Turckheim) in Alsatian tradition?
2.options.0: It was named after a famous local winemaker
2.options.1: The legendary ground where the sun fought a dragon, known as the "land of fire"
2.options.2: It was named for the abundance of a special spice
2.options.3: It was named after a nearby bridge
2.explanation: Brand means "fire", and legend says it was the ground where the sun fought a dragon — the dragon was finally driven into a dark cave, while Brand's wines have shone in the starry sky of Alsace Grand Cru since the Middle Ages. It is the second-largest site in the granite family (57.95 ha).
3.message: Granite family complete! You now know all 8 granite Grand Crus.
3.keyPoints.0: Brand (Turckheim, 57.95 ha): legendary dragon-slaying ground, excellent in all three noble varieties
3.keyPoints.1: Frankstein (Dambach-la-Ville) and Winzenberg (Blienschwiller): guardians of the northern granite belt of Alsace
3.keyPoints.2: Praelatenberg (Kintzheim): gneiss metamorphic base, overlooked by Haut-Kœnigsbourg castle
3.keyPoints.3: Gloeckelberg (Rodern): granite base but more clayey in texture, mainly Pinot Gris / Gewurztraminer
3.keyPoints.4: What the eight granite Grand Crus share: mineral-rich weathered sandy soils, the ideal cradle of Riesling's backbone and delicate aromas
